entries.clue: I superfluously join two banks in which the same cards are issued (9,6)

annotation.definition: in which the same cards are issued
annotation.definitionNote: Both halves describe the answer rather than name it: the first is the bridge speaking as 'I', the second a card game 'in which' the same hands are dealt.

blocks.note: a second, unneeded bridge over a river speaks for itself

blocks.clueFragment: in which the same cards are issued
blocks.note: the tournament form of bridge where every table plays the same deals

annotation.surface: A spare bridge boasts of spanning a river where, oddly, identical playing cards are handed out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Banks' pulls towards money and 'cards' towards credit cards, but the banks are riverbanks and the cards are a deck: the bridge is literal first, then the card game.
annotation.definitionFit: In duplicate bridge the same deals are replayed at every table, so the identical cards are issued to each.

entries.clue: Block a piece of drama making sudden transformation (9)

annotation.definitionNote: An adjective phrase: a Damascene conversion is a sudden transformation.

blocks.note: a dam blocks a river
kept as is
a scene is part of a play

annotation.surface: An actor or censor blocks part of a play that shows a character changing abruptly.
annotation.walkthrough: Damascene refers to Saul's conversion on the road to Damascus, hence any sudden, total change of heart.
annotation.definitionFit: A Damascene moment is an abrupt transformation, like Paul's on the road to Damascus.

entries.clue: On rising exude vigour, 4 across examples here (7)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition points at four across answers in the grid, each a game and so an example of a pastime.

indicatorNotes.On rising: in a down clue, rising means reading bottom to top

blocks.note: to exude is to give off
sap is energy or vitality

annotation.surface: An instruction to get up and show some energy, with a pointer to other clues in the grid.
annotation.walkthrough: The '4 across' is not clue 4 across (there isn't one) but four of the across answers: duplicate bridge, bullet chess, backgammon and crossword puzzle are all pastimes.
annotation.definitionFit: Bridge, chess, backgammon and crosswords are all ways to pass the time, so each is a pastime.

entries.clue: Brood as Guantanamo is extremely tense (8)

indicatorNotes.extremely: take the extremes, the outer letters, of the next word

blocks.note: Guantanamo Bay is in Cuba
the first and last letters of tense

annotation.surface: Someone worries that conditions at Guantanamo are extremely tense.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brood' looks like worrying, but it is the hen's sense: to sit on eggs. 'As Guantanamo' asks where it is, not what it is like.
annotation.definitionFit: To brood is to sit on eggs to hatch them, which is to incubate.

entries.clue: Radical supporter on left (5)

blocks.note: an ally supports you
L = left

annotation.surface: A political extremist is backed by someone on the left wing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Radical' reads as politics, but here it is chemistry: allyl is a radical, a group of atoms that acts as a unit. In a down clue, ALLY sits on top of L.
annotation.definitionFit: Allyl is a chemical radical, the C3H5 group found in allyl alcohol and garlic compounds.

entries.clue: From lectern, offer for sale one or two birds of prey (5-4)

annotation.definition: one or two birds of prey

blocks.note: church lecterns are often carved as an eagle with spread wings
to hawk goods is to sell them

annotation.surface: A preacher at the lectern tries to sell off a raptor or two.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is witty: the eagle-hawk is one bird, but its name is also two birds of prey side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: An eagle-hawk is a single bird of prey whose name joins two others, an eagle and a hawk.

entries.clue: Old widow taking lid off article for repair (6)

indicatorNotes.taking lid off: a lid is the top, so remove the first letter
indicatorNotes.for repair: something sent for repair gets taken apart and rebuilt

blocks.note: ARTICLE without its first letter A

annotation.surface: An elderly widow opens up some object to have it mended.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like it wants A, AN or THE, but here it is the whole word, beheaded and then rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: Relict is an old word for a widow, the one left behind.

entries.clue: Marksman’s expressionless gaze (7)

blocks.note: a dead face or voice shows no feeling
to eye is to gaze at

annotation.surface: A sniper's blank stare.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s is not possessive: it stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone whose eye never misses the target, originally US slang for a crack shot.

entries.clue: Distinctive character of those cycling (5)

indicatorNotes.cycling: the letters go round, the last moving to the front

blocks.note: the final E rotates to the front

annotation.surface: The special personality of cyclists as a group.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Those cycling' reads as people on bikes, but it is the word THOSE being rotated.
annotation.definitionFit: An ethos is the distinctive character or spirit of a group or culture.

entries.clue: Cats for example not normally considered this? (7)

annotation.definition: Cats for example not normally considered this?

blocks.note: the surface means the animals; the setter means the Lloyd Webber stage show, one example of a genre
yowling felines are rarely called tuneful, so the genre's name is also the quality they lack; the question mark flags the pun

annotation.surface: A remark that cats are not known for their singing.
annotation.walkthrough: Cats the Lloyd Webber show is a musical, while real cats, yowling at night, are not thought musical at all.
annotation.definitionFit: Cats is a famous stage musical, and 'musical' is the quality real cats lack.

entries.clue: Turning, pig conceals curly bit, a monster (7)

indicatorNotes.Turning: turning round, so the whole reads backwards
indicatorNotes.conceals: one word hides the other inside it

blocks.note: a hog is a pig; it holds the next piece after H
a pig's curly bit is its tail

annotation.surface: A monstrous pig turns round, hiding its curly tail.
annotation.walkthrough: H(TAIL)OG, read backwards, gives the giant. The surface keeps it all on the pig, so the curly bit is a pig's tail.
annotation.definitionFit: Goliath was the giant slain by David, so any monster of great size.

entries.clue: Indian address the US taxman rejected (3)

indicatorNotes.rejected: to reject is literally to throw back, so the letters are sent back the way they came

blocks.note: the Internal Revenue Service collects US taxes

annotation.surface: An address in India that the American tax authority turned down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Address' is a form of address, not a street location: Sri is an Indian title of respect.
annotation.definitionFit: Sri is an honorific used before names in India, a form of address like Mr.

entries.clue: Revolutionary’s taking ammunition round: very brief opportunity to finish off king here (6,5)

annotation.definition: very brief opportunity to finish off king here
annotation.definitionNote: The definition describes the game rather than naming it: a format so fast there is little time to checkmate.

indicatorNotes.taking: the revolutionary's letters take in, that is are placed in, the ammunition
indicatorNotes.round: the ammunition goes round the other piece

blocks.note: bullets are ammunition; they wrap round the next piece before their final S
Che Guevara, the revolutionary, with his 's

annotation.surface: A revolutionary grabs ammunition and seizes a brief chance to kill the king.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is regicide by a revolutionary; the king is a chess piece. Bullet chess gives each player a minute or so for the whole game.
annotation.definitionFit: In bullet chess each side has about a minute, so there is a very brief window to checkmate the king.

entries.clue: Foolishly let eclair start to curdle in such a storm (10)

annotation.definitionNote: An adjective: an electrical storm; 'in such a storm' asks for the kind of storm.

indicatorNotes.Foolishly: done foolishly, so the letters are jumbled
indicatorNotes.start to: the start of the next word is its first letter

blocks.note: anagram fodder
first letter of curdle

annotation.surface: Someone foolishly lets a cream pastry go off in a thunderstorm, as thunder is said to curdle milk.
annotation.walkthrough: Thunder was once believed to sour milk, which is why curdling cream belongs in a stormy surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A fixed phrase: a storm with lightning is called an electrical storm, so the answer names the kind of storm.

entries.clue: Soon desert old sweetheart (9)

blocks.note: in a mo, short for in a moment
to rat is to desert, as rats leave a sinking ship
O = old

annotation.surface: A former lover who will soon walk out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Desert' is the verb, not sand, and 'in a mo' is British slang for shortly.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym borrowed from Italian, where innamorato means one who has fallen in love; it is the masculine form.

entries.clue: Understood sourdough not provided with starter (4)

indicatorNotes.not provided with starter: a starter is what comes first, as in a meal, so the word is served without its opening letter

blocks.note: BREAD minus its first letter B

annotation.surface: Sourdough made without a starter culture, which a baker knows it needs.
annotation.walkthrough: The pun: sourdough really does need a starter, the fermenting culture, but here the starter is just the letter B of BREAD.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiomatic sense: radio operators say 'I read you' to mean they have understood the message.

entries.clue: Teacher, put my way some work I don’t know (4,3,2)

blocks.note: a don is a university teacher
a task is a piece of work
a task put my way is a task to ME

annotation.surface: A pupil asks the teacher for some work, then admits ignorance.
annotation.walkthrough: A don is a university lecturer, a British usage. The definition sits at the end as a spoken reply, a whole phrase standing for another phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: "Don't ask me" is a common way of saying I don't know.

entries.clue: From people in leading university high-level options here (4,4)

indicatorNotes.in: one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: main means chief or leading
men are people
U = university

annotation.surface: Choices at a senior level made by members of a top university.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leading university' looks like one phrase for a top college, but it splits into two pieces that the people slip between.
annotation.definitionFit: A main menu lists the top-level options in a program or website.

entries.clue: Observer takes in Queen Jane, a heroine (4)

annotation.definitionNote: EYRE is the surname of the heroine Jane, so the definition names her by her first name.

indicatorNotes.takes in: one piece takes the other inside it

blocks.note: an eye observes
R = regina, queen

annotation.surface: A watcher admits Queen Jane to their company, a heroic woman.
annotation.walkthrough: Queen Jane (Lady Jane Grey) is a history reading; split it, and the Queen is R and Jane is the start of Charlotte Brontë's Jane Eyre.
annotation.definitionFit: Jane Eyre is the heroine of Charlotte Brontë's novel.

entries.clue: Cook, first to offer to stir dish (7)

indicatorNotes.Cook: to cook letters is to rearrange them
indicatorNotes.first to: the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: first letter of offer
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Kitchen instructions: the cook must first offer to stir the dish.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a recipe, and a risotto really does need constant stirring.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: this Italian rice preparation is one kind of dish.

entries.clue: Favour cured meat, a somewhat dicey business (10)

blocks.note: to back is to favour
gammon is cured ham

annotation.surface: A preference for cured meat, a slightly risky venture.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dicey' reads as risky, but literally it means played with dice, which backgammon is.
annotation.definitionFit: Backgammon is a board game played with dice, so a dicey business.

entries.clue: Nobel laureate’s emblem unknown (7)

blocks.note: a marque is a brand emblem
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns

annotation.surface: A Nobel prize winner's badge is a mystery.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s is 'is', not possessive. Gabriel García Márquez won the 1982 Nobel Prize in Literature.
annotation.definitionFit: Gabriel García Márquez, the Colombian novelist, won the Nobel Prize for Literature.

entries.clue: Leg straps for James and Norman (6)

blocks.note: in falconry, the short straps fastened to a hawk's legs
Jesse James the outlaw and Jesse Norman the soprano

annotation.surface: Straps worn on the legs by two men named James and Norman.
annotation.walkthrough: James and Norman look like first names; they are surnames, and both people share the first name Jesse.
annotation.definitionFit: In falconry, jesses are the short straps fastened round a hawk's legs.

entries.clue: One small request, excessive space on motorway badly designed (11)

indicatorNotes.on: the other pieces are placed on the motorway, so in an across entry they follow its letter

blocks.note: M = motorway, as in the M1
I = one
S = small
to beg is to request
OTT = over the top
an en is a printer's space

annotation.surface: A complaint about a badly planned motorway with too much room on it.
annotation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on motorway' puts M first, with the other pieces following it. An en is a printer's space, half an em.
annotation.definitionFit: Misbegotten literally means wrongly conceived, and by extension any plan or structure that was badly thought out.

entries.clue: Computer receiving new input initially furiously busy (5)

indicatorNotes.receiving: the first piece receives the others inside it
indicatorNotes.initially: at the start, so only the word's initial letter is used

blocks.note: a Mac is an Apple computer
N = new
first letter of input

annotation.surface: A computer being fed new data at first is working flat out.
annotation.walkthrough: The computing surface makes 'input' look like data; only its first letter is used.
annotation.definitionFit: Manic means frantically, feverishly active.

entries.clue: Ready to drop some older items over (5)

indicatorNotes.some: some of the letters, a run inside the words

blocks.note: the run olDER ITems, which reads backwards

annotation.surface: Some old things are about to fall off, time to hand them over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ready to drop' is exhausted, not something about to fall.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone ready to drop is so worn out they might collapse.

entries.clue: Laundry regularly returned, lots of it in the cells (1,1,1)

annotation.definition: lots of it in the cells

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so letters are picked at a steady stride, one skipped between each
indicatorNotes.returned: laundry is returned to its owner; here the letters are sent back the way they came, last first

blocks.note: the even letters of lAuNdRy

annotation.surface: Laundry that comes back every week, a lot of it for the prison cells.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cells' suggests a prison laundry, but these are living cells, full of ribonucleic acid.
annotation.definitionFit: RNA, ribonucleic acid, is found in large amounts in every living cell.

entries.clue: Possibly a Russian national tree (and American) (7)

blocks.note: NAT = national
the ash is a tree
A = American

annotation.surface: A tree that might be a Russian native, or American.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Russian national' looks like one phrase for a citizen; split it after Russian. 'Possibly' flags that Natasha is one example of a Russian name.
annotation.definitionFit: Natasha is a typical Russian woman's name, so possibly a Russian.

entries.clue: Creature said to take to the water with young on back clinging to side of neck (7)

indicatorNotes.said: spoken, so go by the sound
indicatorNotes.on back: turned onto its back, so reversed
indicatorNotes.side of: one side, here the end, of the next word

blocks.note: to row is to take to the water in a boat
a cub is a young animal
last letter of neck

annotation.surface: An animal swims off with its baby riding on its back, holding onto its neck.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a mother animal carrying her young as she swims; in the wordplay the young is CUB, flipped.
annotation.definitionFit: A roebuck is a male roe deer, a creature.

entries.clue: This bad-tempered oath a mystery (9,6)

blocks.note: cross means angry
to give your word is to swear an oath
a puzzle is a mystery

annotation.surface: A grumpy curse that no one can understand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'This' refers to the thing you are solving, the crossword itself.
annotation.definitionFit: 'This' is the very crossword puzzle the solver is working on.
